sections.overview: Paraswammerdamia lutarea is a small European ermine moth in the family Yponomeutidae. Some British sources use the name P. nebulella for this moth.
sections.identification: The adult is a greyish micro-moth with a pale, usually white head and a wingspan of about 11–14 mm.
sections.habitat: It is associated with hedgerows, woodland margins and open woodland where hawthorn and rowan grow; the available habitat records are mainly regional European accounts.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on leaves of hawthorn and rowan, and have also been recorded on rose and some cotoneasters.
sections.behavior: Adults fly at night and may be attracted to light. The larva first feeds within leaves, then in a loose silk web.
sections.reproduction: In Britain, the small larva overwinters. A Central European study instead reports two generations and overwintering as a pupa, so the cycle may vary among regions or source taxon concepts.
sections.ecology: Its larvae feed on several Rosaceae shrubs and trees, especially hawthorn and rowan, but available accounts do not describe major economic damage.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted report it as fairly common in Britain and locally recorded in continental Europe; they do not establish a global conservation assessment.
